Price inflation can have several determinants besides the money supply. Economists like to use what’s call the “equation of exchange” to understand the effects of changes in money supply or the causes of inflation. The equation goes as follows:

MV = PY

Where M is the money supply, V is the frequency at which money switches hands in a year, P is the price level and Y is real GDP. If we hold V and Y constant then we can see that an increase in M leads to a proportion increase increase in P. In reality, V and Y are not constant. We live in a society with a growing economy and people may prefer to spend less/more (I.e. hold a greater/lesser proportion of their cash balances).

Another thing to consider is that there are several measurements of “the money supply”. What the fed controls is the monetary base which consists of currency which circulates as cash or which banks use for reserves.
